chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Ṭāʾī, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated to me from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام.

He said: I said to him, “A woman or a slave-girl clings to me from behind while I am reclining on my side, and she moves upon my back, then desire comes to her and she emits fluid. Is ghusl (ritual bath) obligatory upon her or not?” He said: “Yes. If desire comes to her and she emits fluid, ghusl becomes obligatory upon her.”

key_terms.الشَّهْوَةُ: sexual desire whose occurrence is part of the described condition
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةُ: a slave-girl mentioned as also subject to the same ruling
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath that becomes obligatory
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: the emitted fluid referred to in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman in question regarding the ruling

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory upon a woman according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that ghusl (ritual bath) becomes obligatory upon a woman when sexual desire occurs and she emits fluid, whether in a circumstance of bodily contact while awake or otherwise. Its significance in fiqh is the clarification that the ruling of janabah applies upon actual emission together with shahwah.
